title: External Secant and Tangent Angles Assessment
description: Show mastery of secant-secant, tangent-tangent, and tangent-secant exterior angle cases.

questions.question: Two secants from an exterior point intercept arcs of 184° and 76°. What is the exterior angle?
A tangent and a secant form an exterior angle. The larger intercepted arc is 230° and the smaller arc is 90°. Find the angle.
Two tangents touch a circle at points that cut off a minor arc of 64°. What is the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: For two tangents, angle = 180 - minor arc = 180 - 64 = 116°.

questions.question: If a tangent-tangent exterior angle is 90°, then the minor arc between the tangent points is also 90°.
questions.explanation: For two tangents, angle = 180 - minor arc. If the angle is 90°, then the minor arc is 90°.

questions.question: A secant-secant exterior angle intercepts arcs of 125° and 35°. Enter the angle measure in degrees.
An exterior angle is 42°. The smaller intercepted arc is 58°. What is the larger intercepted arc?
Two tangents form an exterior angle of 36°. What is the minor arc between the tangent points?
questions.explanation: 36 = 180 - minor arc, so the minor arc is 144°.

questions.question: A tangent-secant angle intercepts arcs of 246° and 114°. Enter the exterior angle measure in degrees.
The exterior angle formed by a tangent and a secant can be found with the same half-difference formula used for two secants.
questions.explanation: Both secant-secant and tangent-secant exterior angles use half the difference of intercepted arcs.

questions.question: A secant-secant exterior angle measures 25°. The larger arc is 150°. What is the smaller arc?
Two tangents form an exterior angle. The major arc between the tangent points is 280°. Find the exterior angle and explain your steps.
questions.correctAnswer: The minor arc is 360 - 280 = 80°. The exterior angle is 1/2(280 - 80) = 100°, or 180 - 80 = 100°.
questions.explanation: Tangent-tangent problems use the major and minor arcs between the tangent points.

questions.question: A learner claims that arcs 210° and 40° give an exterior angle of 125° because 210 + 40 = 250 and half of 250 is 125. Correct the reasoning.
questions.correctAnswer: Exterior secant and tangent angles use half the difference of intercepted arcs, not half the sum. The correct angle is 1/2(210 - 40) = 85°.
questions.explanation: The key relationship is half the difference between the larger and smaller intercepted arcs.
